items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: And Joe Caprera, man. That band used to rock like that, man.

ctx.x: What about waltzes? How many waltzes would you play?

Oh man, the piano player had a big chord in front, you couldn't think that quick, you know, like waltzes would be like an A flat or B flat or B flat or A flat, when it was, you go right into a waltz, see, usually, Let Me Call Your Sweetheart or Girl Of My Dreams or, there wasn't too much of a right to waltzes. We would play, you know, just one every fourth piece would play, and the band would take a rest, see, and then the piano player would play, and then, see, on the other tune, played, this tune goes shocked,…

Did you ever play underneath Hawaiian skies? You know that, uh... Foozie Rye's about the only one I know around that knows it today. If I hear it, what? Raymond knows it. If she'd turn the machine off, I'd try to sing it. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
